messages.text: How do changes in Wi-Fi 7/8 technology affect the measurement capability required from Signal Generator / Signal Analyzer?

Wi-Fi 8 keeps Wi-Fi 7’s cited core PHY envelope: supported frequencies up to 7.125 GHz, channel bandwidths up to 320 MHz, 4096QAM, and MLO [25].
Wi-Fi 8 adds UHR-oriented IEEE 802.11bn PHY/MAC technologies, and the raw source says these create new testing hurdles [25].
The raw tester evidence says the needed platform class supports data rates up to 20 Gbps, wide dynamic range, 4096QAM, and up to 16 device antenna ports for advanced spatial multiplexing [26].
The same raw evidence says the platform is multiband and covers WLAN including Wi‑Fi 7 and future Wi‑Fi 8 [26].
Wi‑Fi 7 R&D raw evidence is limited to the statement that CMX500 has new Wi‑Fi 7 capabilities for R&D [28].
【推論】Required Signal Generator capability: generate/signaling Wi‑Fi waveforms for up to 7.125 GHz operation, 320 MHz channels, 4096QAM, MLO or multiband cases, and multi-antenna spatial-multiplexing scenarios up to the 16-device-antenna-port class evidenced for the tester platform [25][26].
【推論】Required Signal Analyzer capability: analyze high-data-rate Wi‑Fi 7 / Wi‑Fi 8 transmissions up to the 20 Gbps class, with wide dynamic range, 4096QAM handling, multiband/MLO coverage, and multi-antenna spatial-multiplexing analysis up to the 16-device-antenna-port class [25][26].
